title: Windows platform backend: clipboard, hotkeys, paste pipeline
setup: Start this wizard from a normal (non-admin) window and snap it to the left half of the screen (Win+Left).
Turn on clipboard history: press Win+V, then 'Turn on' (needed to check that pasted items never show up there).
Open a normal (non-admin) Notepad. Have Word, Chrome (signed in to Gmail), Paint, an Explorer folder and Windows Terminal ready. Optional: OneNote, Remote Desktop, Ditto or CopyQ, PowerToys.

The harness has no window; it registers global hotkeys: Ctrl+Alt+1 paste text, 2 HTML, 3 plain, 4 copy, 5 PNG, 6 files, 7 print Target info, 8 long unicode, Q quit. Focus the target app BEFORE pressing a chord and hold the keys until the paste happens (that exercises the Alt mask).
It never prints clipboard content or window titles (title length only). 'l' shows its log.

tests.title: Start-up report
tests.do: Press 'l' to read the harness log.
tests.expect: windows= and integrity=not elevated. dpapi=ok (round-trip=True, wrong-entropy-rejected=True). chords line: Ctrl+Alt+1 parses, Shift+A and A are rejected. instance=first. 'hotkeys registered=9 in-use=0 errors=0' plus one 'registered' line per chord. If a chord is InUse, record which.

tests.title: Notepad: paste, clipboard restored
tests.do: In a normal Notepad type abc and leave the caret there (the wizard put BEFORE on the clipboard). Press Ctrl+Alt+1 and keep both keys down until the text appears. Then press Ctrl+V. Open Win+V.
tests.expect: 'Hello from Snipdeck M2' inserted at the caret. Log: use=Paste target=notepad.exe focus=Caret route=paste(CtrlV) outcome=Pasted. Ctrl+V then pastes BEFORE. Win+V history does NOT contain the item. No stuck Ctrl or Alt.

tests.title: Alt and Win held: no menu hints, no Start menu
tests.do: In Notepad: hold Alt, then press Ctrl+1 (the chord) and keep Alt down for a second after the text appears; release. Repeat holding Ctrl+Alt+1 together. S1 2c again: hold the Windows key, press Ctrl+Alt+1 with Win still down, release all.
tests.expect: Pasted each time (Win+chord may not match the hotkey: if nothing happens, record it, it is not a failure by itself). Notepad's menu bar is NOT activated (no underlined access keys). Start menu does NOT open on releasing Win. Typing afterwards is normal.

tests.title: HTML into Word and Gmail compose
tests.do: Word: click into a blank document, press Ctrl+Alt+2. Chrome: Gmail compose (rich text), click into the body, Ctrl+Alt+2.
tests.expect: Both show a red heading 'Snipdeck M2 HTML', bold, italic and a working link. Log: outcome=Pasted. The previous clipboard is back afterwards (Ctrl+V into Notepad).

tests.title: Plain paste (HTML item as text)
tests.do: In Word, then in Gmail compose, press Ctrl+Alt+3.
tests.expect: Only 'Plain text of the HTML item': no heading, bold or link. Log: use=PastePlain outcome=Pasted.

tests.title: Copy mode leaves the item on the clipboard
tests.do: In Notepad press Ctrl+Alt+4. Then press Ctrl+V.
tests.expect: The hotkey inserts nothing. Log: use=Copy outcome=Copied. Ctrl+V pastes 'Hello from Snipdeck M2' (not restored away). Note whether Win+V shows it (Copy is an ordinary copy, so it may).

tests.title: PNG into Paint, Word and Chrome
tests.do: Paint: new canvas, Ctrl+Alt+5. Word: blank document, Ctrl+Alt+5. Chrome: Gmail compose body (or a GitHub comment), Ctrl+Alt+5.
tests.expect: A 64x64 picture: four colour quadrants, black frame. The top-left 20x20 corner is WHITE in Paint (not black, not magenta). In Word and Chrome record white or transparent; magenta means alpha is ignored. Log: outcome=Pasted.

tests.title: Files into an Explorer folder
tests.do: Open an empty Explorer folder, click an empty spot, press Ctrl+Alt+6.
tests.expect: m2-note-1.txt and m2-note-2.txt appear, containing 'M2 file one' / 'two'. Log: target=explorer.exe outcome=Pasted. Pressing it in Notepad should insert no text (record what happens).

tests.title: Long multi-line unicode text
tests.do: In Notepad press Ctrl+Alt+8 and scroll through.
tests.expect: Starts BEGIN-M2-TEXT, ends END-M2-TEXT, 40 'Line NN' lines intact: German, CJK, Korean, Arabic, check mark, euro, combining accent, emoji, family emoji; a blank line and a tab-indented line at the end. Log: ms is low.

tests.title: Windows Terminal and OneNote
tests.do: Click into Windows Terminal (PowerShell prompt), press Ctrl+Alt+7, then Ctrl+Alt+1. Repeat in OneNote (click into a page).
tests.expect: Ctrl+Alt+7 prints 'target app=WindowsTerminal.exe title_len=<n> elevated=False focus=Automation' (or Control: record which) and never the title. The terminal paste logs route=paste(CtrlShiftV) and the text appears. OneNote: app=ONENOTE.EXE, focus Automation or Control, paste works. focus=None would mean a copy fallback: record it.

tests.title: Elevated Notepad: copy fallback
tests.do: Run Notepad as administrator, click into it, press Ctrl+Alt+7, Ctrl+Alt+1, then Ctrl+V.
tests.expect: Info shows elevated=True. The hotkey types nothing. Log: route=copy(Elevated) outcome=CopiedInstead(TargetElevated). Ctrl+V then pastes 'Hello from Snipdeck M2'. (The user-facing message is the app's job; record the outcome name.)

tests.title: Remote Desktop: slow target
tests.do: Connect Remote Desktop (even to another PC), click into Notepad inside it, press Ctrl+Alt+1.
tests.expect: Record whether the remote side gets the item or the OLD clipboard, and ms=. outcome is Pasted or CopiedInstead(TargetUnavailable); no hang, no stuck keys.

tests.title: Clipboard changed mid-paste is not overwritten
tests.do: The wizard relaunched the harness with --clobber (a second clipboard owner writes 'Written by another app mid-paste' right after the Target pastes). BEFORE is on the clipboard. In Notepad press Ctrl+Alt+1, then Ctrl+V.
tests.expect: Log: 'clobber: another owner wrote newer content ok=True', outcome=Pasted. Ctrl+V pastes 'Written by another app mid-paste', NOT BEFORE: the restore refused to overwrite newer content.

tests.title: Clipboard manager records nothing
tests.do: Start Ditto or CopyQ and clear its history. In Notepad press Ctrl+Alt+1, 2, 5 and 6 (harness relaunched normally). Look at the manager. Then press Ctrl+Alt+4.
tests.expect: The manager records none of the pasted items, nor the restored previous clipboard (privacy markers). Ctrl+Alt+4 is an ordinary copy and may be recorded: note it. If the manager ignores the markers, record it as a limitation.

tests.title: Single instance: later launches raise the first
tests.do: With the harness running, open a terminal and run tools\windows-test\m2-harness\target\release\m2-harness.exe three times in a row, quickly. Press 'l'.
tests.expect: Each launch prints '[m2] second instance' and exits. The harness log gains three '[m2] raised' lines. Hotkeys still work.

tests.title: Autostart on and off
tests.do: The wizard ran the harness with --autostart-test --hold 25. Within 25 s look in regedit at HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for the value 'Snipdeck', then refresh after the app exits. It uses the real value name: run it only where no real Snipdeck is installed (it removes that value).
tests.expect: Log: 'set on -> is_enabled=Ok(true)', 'set off -> is_enabled=Ok(false)', 'autostart=ok'. In regedit 'Snipdeck' holds the quoted path of m2-harness.exe while held and is gone afterwards.

tests.title: Hotkey conflict reports InUse
tests.do: The wizard launched the harness with --probe Win+L. Read the log ('l'). With PowerToys installed also relaunch by hand with --probe Win+Shift+C (Color Picker default) while it runs.
tests.expect: 'hotkey Win+L InUse (another app owns it)' and in-use=1; the nine real hotkeys still register. With PowerToys running Win+Shift+C is InUse too. No crash.

tests.title: Quit leaves hotkeys free
tests.do: Relaunch normally (r). Press Ctrl+Alt+Q. Read the log, press Ctrl+Alt+1 in Notepad, then start the exe again (r).
tests.expect: Log ends '[m2] quit: hotkeys released' and the process exits. Ctrl+Alt+1 does nothing now. The next launch reports in-use=0.

tests.title: Windows backend unit tests
tests.do: In a terminal at the repo root run: cargo test -p snipdeck-platform -- --ignored clipboard   (it uses and overwrites your real clipboard)
tests.expect: 6 tests run (the ignored Windows-only clipboard tests) and all pass.
